title: Punctured Disks, Mapping Classes, and Point Pushing

items.title: Boundary-fixed mapping class group of a punctured disk
items.statement: For the fixed Q_n, Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) is π₀ of the compact-open group of orientation-preserving disk homeomorphisms that fix ∂D² pointwise and preserve Q_n setwise; paths are isotopies subject to both conditions. Multiplication is ordinary composition.
items.proof_strategy: Use the interval exponential law to identify compact-open paths with ambient isotopies; prove composition and inversion continuous in the compact-open/uniform topology on homeomorphisms of compact D².

items.title: Pure boundary-fixed mapping classes
items.statement: PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) consists of the classes represented by homeomorphisms fixing every q_i; isotopies fix each q_i and ∂D² throughout.
items.proof_strategy: The pointwise stabilizer is a subgroup and a path in the setwise stabilizer has constant permutation of the finite marked set, so setwise and pointwise isotopy conventions coincide for pure representatives.

items.title: Alexander contraction of the boundary-fixed disk homeomorphism group
items.statement: Homeo⁺(D²,∂D²), with the compact-open topology, is contractible.
items.proof_strategy: For 0<s≤1 set H_s(h)(x)=s h(x/s) for |x|≤s and x otherwise; H_0(h)=id. At |x|=s the formulas agree because h fixes the circle. Uniform distance to id is at most 2s; for s>0 uniform continuity proves joint continuity in (s,h).

items.title: Continuous local sections for disk point evaluation
items.statement: For evaluation ev:Homeo⁺(D²,∂D²)→C_n(int D²), h↦h(Q_n), every configuration has a neighborhood with a continuous section; ev is onto, including n=0.
items.proof_strategy: In disjoint disks choose Lipschitz cutoffs χ_i equal to one at the points. For small displacement v_i, h_i(x)=x+χ_i(x)v_i has Lip(h_i-id)<1; Banach fixed point proves its global inverse. Compose disjoint supports. Path connectivity of ordered configurations and a finite partition of a path give an ambient homeomorphism sending Q_n to any target; translate the local formula by it.

items.title: Smooth relative isotopy extension for finite disk arc systems
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. A smooth isotopy of one compact embedded proper arc, stationary on collars of its fixed endpoints and disjoint from prescribed marked points and already fixed arcs away from those collars, extends to a smooth ambient disk isotopy fixing ∂D², all marked points, and the fixed arcs; finite successive arc isotopies extend by composition.
items.proof_strategy: By smoothness on the compact time interval, extend F_t in time to a slightly larger open interval. Stationarity on endpoint collars permits a smooth extension of the arc parameter across its endpoints. The resulting time-space track is an embedded submanifold without boundary in R×R²; the published vector-extension lemma applies locally to (0,∂_tF_t). Its velocity is supported on a compact subtrack away from the endpoint collars. Use a smooth cutoff equal to one there and supported inside the extension neighborhood while avoiding the fixed marked points, fixed arcs and disk boundary; take the spatial component and integrate its compactly supported time-dependent field. Uniqueness carries the original arc at every t. The published vector-extension and smooth cutoff results spend AC_ω.

items.title: Evaluation is a numerable bundle and Hurewicz fibration
items.statement: Assume AC. Evaluation Homeo⁺(D²,∂D²)→C_n(int D²) is a locally trivial bundle with fiber Homeo⁺(D²,∂D²;Q_n), is numerable, and hence is a Hurewicz fibration.
items.proof_strategy: For n=0 the base is a point and the assertion is immediate. For n≥1 a local section s gives the product chart h↦(h(Q_n),s(h(Q_n))⁻¹h). The quotient metric min_σ max_i|x_i-y_{σi}| metrizes the finite-permutation quotient. AC implies DC, so the metric partition theorem supplies support-subordinate numerating data; the published numerable-bundle theorem uses AC to well-order finite chart words.

items.title: Boundary map from point motions
items.statement: Assume AC. For a based configuration loop α, lift α under evaluation from id, let h be the endpoint, and set δ([α])=[h⁻¹] in Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²); this is the library’s first-loop-then-second LES convention.
items.proof_strategy: Record the inverse endpoint because the published fibration connecting map is the initial fiber component of a reversed lift; independence and homomorphism are proved in the next lemma.

items.title: Point-motion boundary map is a homomorphism
items.statement: Assume AC. The map δ:π₁(C_n(int D²),[Q_n])→Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) is independent of loop representative and chosen evaluation lift and preserves first-loop-then-second multiplication.
items.proof_strategy: Use square homotopy lifting to compare endpoints in the same fiber component. For loops α then β and chosen lifts a_t,b_t from id, the concatenated lift has endpoint b_1a_1, hence δ(αβ)=[a_1⁻¹b_1⁻¹]=δ(α)δ(β). The LES reverse-lift convention agrees.

items.title: Evaluation boundary isomorphism for the disk
items.statement: Assume AC. δ:π₁(C_n(int D²),[Q_n])→Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²) is an isomorphism for every n≥0.
items.proof_strategy: The low-degree fibration exact sequence has π₁(E)=π₀(E)=0 by the Alexander contraction. Its connecting map is therefore a pointed-set bijection; the preceding lemma makes it a group homomorphism.

items.title: Smooth representatives of configuration loops
items.statement: Every based loop of C_n(int D²) at [Q_n] is homotopic rel endpoints to one whose unique ordered lift from Q_n consists of smooth collision-free coordinate paths constant near t=0,1.
items.proof_strategy: For n=0 use the unique constant loop. Otherwise lift uniquely from Q_n. Compactness gives a positive minimum of all existing pair separations and boundary distances (for n=1 only the latter). Approximate both real coordinates uniformly by polynomials and correct endpoint values by affine interpolation. Use the published smooth step σ to define, for small ε<1/3, a smooth time map λ(t)=tσ(t/ε)σ((1−t)/ε)+1−σ((1−t)/ε). It equals 0 near t=0, 1 near t=1, t on [ε,1−ε], lies in [0,1], and differs from t by at most ε. Uniform continuity keeps p_i(λ(t)) close to the original path. Straight interpolation remains collision-free and away from the boundary under a quarter-margin error; its quotient is the desired based homotopy.

items.title: Smooth finite point motions extend to disk isotopies
items.statement: Assume AC_ω. Every smooth collision-free finite point motion in int D², constant near its time endpoints, extends to a smooth ambient isotopy of D² fixing ∂D² pointwise; the endpoint is a boundary-fixed diffeomorphism carrying the initial marked set to the terminal one.
items.proof_strategy: Extend the paths constantly beyond the time interval. Choose a common positive separation/boundary margin and a smooth Euclidean bump supported in disks below a third of it. Set X_t(x)=Σ_iρ(x-z_i(t)) z_i′(t); supports are disjoint and compact in int D². The global evolution exists, fixes the boundary, and uniqueness makes its tracks equal the given z_i. Countable choice is declared because the published time-dependent vector-field definition uses it, although the finite Euclidean construction itself makes no arbitrary selection.

items.title: Braid group as boundary-fixed punctured-disk mapping classes
items.statement: Assume AC. The geometric braid group on Q_n is canonically isomorphic to Mod(D²,Q_n;∂D²), sending the standard geometric half twist to its disk-supported mapping class; every mapping class has a boundary-fixed smooth representative.
items.proof_strategy: Compose the published inverse-slicing isomorphism Φ:G_n→π₁(C_n(D²),[Q_n]) with the inverse of the published open-to-closed configuration isomorphism ι^C_* and then with the inverse-endpoint boundary δ on π₁(C_n(int D²),[Q_n]). For a geometric braid the inverse slicing and inverse endpoint cancel, so its smooth point-motion endpoint represents the image and a positive adjacent half rotation gives the supported positive half twist. Smooth-approximate an open-disk configuration loop rel endpoints and integrate the finite disjoint bump field to represent every class smoothly.

items.title: Pure braids as pure mapping classes
items.statement: Assume AC. Under the braid–mapping-class isomorphism, the pure geometric braid subgroup equals PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²).
items.proof_strategy: The evaluation endpoint homeomorphism has the same point permutation as the raw point motion; Φ and δ each invert it. Compare kernels of the resulting maps to S_n.

items.title: Point pushing the last puncture
items.statement: Assume AC and n≥1. Holding q_1,…,q_{n−1} fixed, an n-th-point loop in int D²\{q_1,…,q_{n−1}} gives an ordered configuration loop, and its inverse-endpoint evaluation boundary class defines Push_n into PMod(D²,Q_n;∂D²). No injectivity claim is made here.
items.proof_strategy: Compose the coordinate inclusion of the puncture complement with the ordered-to-unordered quotient and δ. The fixed coordinates force identity permutation, hence a pure class. The homomorphism property is inherited from δ; leave its kernel to BG-5 after π₂(F_{n−1}(D²)) vanishes.

title: Punctured Disks, Mapping Classes, and Point Pushing — Examples

items.title: A supported half-twist homeomorphism
items.statement: Assume AC. For adjacent q_i,q_{i+1}, a disk-supported angular half rotation with collar interpolation exchanges the two punctures and represents the standard positive braid generator.
items.proof_strategy: In the support disk centered at their midpoint, rotate through π on a smaller disk containing both points, taper the angle smoothly to 0 in an outer collar, and use the time-scaled rotations. Their point paths are anticlockwise semicircles isotopic to the published diamond half twist.

items.title: Point pushing one puncture around another
items.statement: Assume AC. For n=2, clockwise pushing q_2 once around fixed q_1 gives the positive pure two-strand full twist, the square of the published positive half twist; counterclockwise pushing gives its inverse.
items.proof_strategy: The clockwise fixed-first-point path has difference coordinate (q_2−q_1)e^{-2πit}. The raw open-disk point motion of the square of the published positive half twist has counterclockwise difference winding; its inverse is clockwise. Linearly interpolate center coordinates to show the push loop is homotopic in the open-disk ordered configuration space to that inverse raw slice. The published open-to-closed isomorphism identifies this open class with ι_*^{-1}Φ(σ_1²), so applying δ gives the positive full-twist mapping class. Reversing the push loop gives its inverse.

items.title: Setwise boundary preservation kills a nontrivial braid
items.statement: Assume AC. For n=2, replacing pointwise boundary fixing throughout isotopies by setwise boundary preservation makes a nontrivial full twist trivial.
items.proof_strategy: Rigidly rotate the whole disk through 2π: the endpoint is id and the boundary is only preserved setwise during the isotopy. On unordered two-point configurations define u({x,y})=((x−y)/|x−y|)^2 in the complex plane; swapping x,y changes the normalized difference by −1 and leaves u fixed, so the quotient universal property makes u continuous. The rigid-rotation loop maps under u to a circle loop of degree 2, hence is not nullhomotopic. The boundary-fixed evaluation isomorphism makes its mapping class nontrivial.

items.title: Setwise puncture preservation does not imply purity
items.statement: Assume AC. A supported positive half twist preserves Q_n as a set but exchanges q_i and q_{i+1}, hence is not a pure mapping class when n≥2.
items.proof_strategy: Read the explicit supported half rotation of the preceding example: it swaps exactly the adjacent pair. An isotopy through setwise Q_n-preserving homeomorphisms cannot change this discrete permutation.
